name: Ganyushu granule (Chinese herbal formula)
short: One placebo-controlled trial, 240 women with premenstrual syndrome (by mouth, up to 3 cycles): no serious adverse reactions reported; no other adverse-event figures given. Herbs not listed.
text: Ganyushu granule is a Chinese herbal formula taken by mouth; the cited abstract does not list its herbs. In a randomized, double-blind, multicentre phase II trial, 240 women with premenstrual syndrome were divided into a higher-dose group, a lower-dose group and a placebo group for up to 3 menstrual cycles, and clinical safety was assessed; no serious adverse reactions were reported. The abstract gives no other adverse-event figures and does not compare adverse-event rates between the groups, so it does not show how often milder side effects occurred; the authors conclude that the granules were safe and well tolerated at both doses, but the abstract gives no event counts behind this. No other human safety data were found in PubMed searches under the formula's names. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.

citations.label: Teng et al., 2024, Chin J Integr Med
citations.title: Efficacy and Safety of Ganyushu Granule in Treatment of Premenstrual Syndrome with Gan (Liver) Depression and Qi Stagnation Syndrome: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Multicenter, Phase-II Clinical Trial.
